record.original_question: For the complete graph K_n, is the planar crossing number equal to (1/4)·floor(n/2)·floor((n−1)/2)·floor((n−2)/2)·floor((n−3)/2)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K_n$ denote the complete graph on $n$ vertices. The (planar) crossing number $\mathrm{cr}(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the minimum, over all drawings of $G$ in the plane with vertices represented by distinct points and edges by continuous curves joining their endpoints (such that no edge passes through a vertex other than its endpoints, no two edges sharing an endpoint cross, and no two edges cross more than once), of the number of pairs of edges that cross.

Determine whether, for every integer $n \geq 1$,
$$\mathrm{cr}(K_n) \;=\; \frac{1}{4}\left\lfloor \frac{n}{2} \right\rfloor \left\lfloor \frac{n-1}{2} \right\rfloor \left\lfloor \frac{n-2}{2} \right\rfloor \left\lfloor \frac{n-3}{2} \right\rfloor.$$
artifact.status_search_result: Known as Guy's conjecture. The formula is a proven upper bound (Hill; Blažek–Koman). Equality has been verified for n ≤ 12 (Guy for small n; Pan–Richter 2007 for n = 11, 12), which by parity also gives n = 13. For general n the conjecture remains open; the best known lower bound is cr(K_n) ≥ 0.8594 Z(n).
